# Goal

Fix the audit runner's parent-first flow so that child `partial` verdicts caused by unserviced in-main-slot items are treated as "not assessed" rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision, and add diagnostic clarity.

# Background

In `--child-in-main-slot` mode (default), child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session. In non-interactive runs (e.g. downtime workers), these items are never serviced, leaving all child AC verdicts as `partial`.

Currently, `_build_issue_json` treats ALL `partial` verdicts as unacceptable, causing the parent to report "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met, because the child partials (from unserviced in-main-slot work) are counted as failures.

# Implementation Plan

## 1. Track in-main-slot partial verdicts

Add a `verdict_reason` field to child AC results when they are `partial` due to in-main-slot unserviced work. The `_phase1_review_child_acs` and `_deep_analyze_child` functions already set `verdict: "partial"` with evidence like `"pending (main-session review)"` in in-main-slot mode. We need to mark these explicitly with `verdict_reason: "unserviced-in-main-slot"`.

## 2. Handle partials in `_build_issue_json`

Modify `all_ac_acceptable` computation to skip child ACs whose `partial` verdict has `verdict_reason == "unserviced-in-main-slot"`. These should be treated as "not assessed" and NOT block the parent's readiness-to-close decision.

## 3. Add diagnostic output

In the audit summary/JSON output, surface a clear diagnostic that distinguishes:
- Children with `partial` verdicts from unserviced in-main-slot work → "not assessed"
- Children with genuine `partial` or `unmet` verdicts → "not-ready"

Add a `children_assessment` section to the `_build_issue_json` output listing `unserviced_in_main_slot` child IDs and `genuine_not_ready` child IDs.

# Acceptance Criteria
- AC2: Parent audit treats in-main-slot unserviced partials as "not assessed" (does NOT block ready-to-close)
- AC3: Audit output includes diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot partials from genuine failures

# Constraints
- Must not change behaviour of interactive runs (where agent CAN service in-main-slot items)
- Must be backward-compatible with persisted audit results

# Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase1_review_child_acs`, `_deep_analyze_child`, `_build_issue_json`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — existing in-main-slot tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — freshness tests (verify no regression)
data.title: Fix in-main-slot partial verdict handling and diagnostics (AC2-AC3)

# Enemy gym: P3 shield and P6 phase shift do not work when collected (hit-gating not shared)

## Seed intent (operator)

In the enemies gym scene some power-ups — at least phase shift (P6) and shield (P3) — do not work when collected. This suggests these scenes (at least the diver) are not using the same code as other scenes. Perform a root-cause analysis and ensure shared code is used so behaviour is the same in all scenes.

## Raw evidence

- Operator report: collecting P6 Phase Shift or P3 Shield in the enemy gym has no observable defensive effect (player still takes hits).
- Hint: 'at least the diver' — the Diver is an enemy-config key routed to the single reusable `GymEnemies` scene (GymIndex boots `GymEnemies` with `{ enemyKey }` for every non-boss enemy config).

## Problem statement

In the enemy gym scene (`GymEnemies`, used for every enemy config including the
Diver), collecting P3 Shield or P6 Phase Shift has no defensive effect: the
player still takes hits and loses a life. The effects are recorded in the shared
`EffectsRegistry` (the standalone HUD shows them active), but the shared combat
base's hit path never consults them for the formation-gym scenes, so the player
is not actually shielded or phased.

## Root cause analysis

- `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` each **override** `isPlayerPhased()` and
  `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` to consult their `EffectsRegistry`.
- `GymFormationScene` (the base for `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`) does
  **not** override either hook, so it inherits the `CombatCoreScene` defaults
  `isPlayerPhased() → false` and `tryAbsorbPlayerHit() → false`.
- `CombatScene._handleCollisions()` calls `isPlayerPhased()` before the
  bullet-vs-player and body-vs-player passes, and `CombatScene._hitPlayer()`
  calls `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` first. Both return the defaults in the formation
  gyms, so P3/P6 never gate a hit.
- Consequently the single reusable enemy gym scene (`GymEnemies` with
  `{ enemyKey }`, e.g. `diver`) records the collected effect but behaves
  differently from `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` — a divergence from the
  documented shared-core invariant in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §2.1 ("The shipped game and the gyms therefore cannot diverge on collision,
  auto-fire, drops, teleport or player-hit behaviour").
- Other power-ups are unaffected and confirm the diagnosis: P4 Bomb works
  (`_collectDrop` → shared `_clearEnemyBullets()`, wired through
  `getEnemyBullets()`/`setEnemyBullets()`); P5/P9 speed and fire-rate
  multipliers are applied in `GymFormationScene` (~line 1209); P7 Teleport works
  via the shared `_handleTeleport()`.
- Secondary divergence: `GymFormationScene` draws no shield bubble or phase
  ghost, so even once gating is fixed the player has no on-screen cue that P3/P6
  is active, unlike `PlayScene`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`.

## Users (user stories)

- As a player training against enemies in the enemy gym, when I fly over a P6
  Phase Shift drop I expect to pass through enemy bullets and enemy bodies
  without being hit, exactly as in the real run.
- As a player training in the enemy gym, when I fly over a P3 Shield drop I
  expect the next hit to be absorbed (one hit), with the shield popping and a
  brief invulnerability blink, without losing a life.
- As a maintainer, I expect phase/shield hit-gating to live in one shared place
  so a fix in one scene cannot silently miss the others.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — P6 phase immunity in the enemy gym:** With the power-up layer active in `GymEnemies` (any `enemyKey`, including `diver`), collecting P6 Phase Shift makes the player immune to enemy bullets and enemy body contact for the effect duration (no `playerHitCount` increment, no life loss, no respawn); on expiry the next hit lands normally. Verified by an automated test on a `GymFormationScene`-based scene.
- [ ] **AC2 — P3 shield absorbs one hit in the enemy gym:** Collecting P3 Shield causes exactly the next hit to be absorbed: the shield is consumed (registry no longer shielded), the post-hit invulnerability window starts, and the player does not lose a life; the following hit lands normally. Verified by an automated test on a `GymFormationScene`-based scene.
- [ ] **AC3 — single shared implementation:** Phase/shield hit-gating is implemented once in the shared combat base (`CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`) backed by the inherited `EffectsRegistry`; the now-redundant duplicate overrides in `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` are removed or reduced to scene-specific extras (e.g. per-type cue/VFX), and an equivalence test asserts `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` route phase/shield through the same shared hooks.
- [ ] **AC4 — consistent player feedback:** `GymFormationScene`-based scenes render the same shield-bubble (P3) and phase-ghost (P6) player visuals as `PlayScene`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`, so the active effect is observable in the enemy gym.
- [ ] **AC5 — documentation:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (and any other docs describing power-up/hit behaviour) is updated to state that shield/phase gating is shared and lists the new shared hooks.
- [ ] **AC6 — validation:** An automated test/validation criterion is satisfied across the affected scenes (new regression tests fail before the fix and pass after it).
- [ ] **AC7 — full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- All implementation must happen in the worktree created by
  `implement.py start`; build → test → commit order, never reversed.
- Do not regress the shipped game: `PlayScene` invulnerability duration
  (`PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE`, 1.5 s) and `GymPowerUpsCombat`
  (`COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION`, 0.8 s) must be preserved; shield-absorb
  must still pop the shield and start invulnerability.
- Preserve the existing shield/lives flow in `PlayScene` (shield absorb must not
  cost a life; an unabsorbed hit still runs the normal lose-life flow).
- No unrelated refactors; keep changes surgical and match existing style.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (release pipeline owns it); do not touch CI/CD.
- Written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — default `isPlayerPhased()` returns
  `false`; default `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` returns `false`; `getEffectsRegistry()`
  returns a private `defaultEffectsRegistry`; `_collectDrop()` applies
  P3/P6 via `registry.applyCollect(drop.dropId)` and clears bullets for P4.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` calls
  `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` then `onPlayerHit()`; `_handleCollisions()` skips
  bullet/body hits when `isPlayerPhased()`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — overrides `isPlayerPhased()` (line ~1083) and
  `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (line ~1245, shield pop + `_startInvulnerability`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — overrides `isPlayerPhased()` (~504)
  and `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (~514).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — owns its `effectsRegistry` and
  HUD; overrides `getEffectsRegistry()` only; **no** phase/shield overrides and
  **no** shield-bubble/phase-ghost visuals.
- `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals` extend `GymFormationScene`; `GymIndex`
  routes every non-boss enemy config (including `diver`) to `GymEnemies`.

## Desired change

- Add registry-backed default `isPlayerPhased()` and `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()`
  (shield absorb → consume shield → start invulnerability → return `true`) to
  the shared combat base, so every `CombatScene` subclass inherits correct
  gating exactly once.
- Reduce `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` overrides to any genuinely
  scene-specific extras; otherwise delete them.
- Add the shared shield-bubble/phase-ghost rendering to `GymFormationScene`
  (or a shared combat visual) for feedback parity.
- Add regression tests proving AC1–AC3 and an equivalence test for the shared
  hook routing.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — registry-backed default
  `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (or move to `CombatScene` if a
  `Player` param is needed for the absorb VFX); document the shared gating.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — keep `_hitPlayer()`/`_handleCollisions()`
  unchanged; host any shared shield-pop cue/visual seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — inherit gating; add shield
  bubble + phase ghost visuals for parity.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — remove/trim now-redundant overrides.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — remove/trim now-redundant overrides.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts` / `CombatScene.test.ts` — shared
  gating unit tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` / `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
  — enemy-gym regression tests (phase immunity, shield absorb).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — assert shared hook routing.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document shared shield/phase gating.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the operator's "continue" authorises the recommended shared-base
  approach and visual-parity scope (Q1/Q2 above); if review disagrees, only the
  de-duplication extent and the visual work change, not AC1–AC3.
- **Risk — shipped-game regression:** moving shield/phase gating into the base
  touches `PlayScene`; mitigated by preserving invulnerability durations and the
  shield/lives flow and by equivalence tests (AC3, AC7).
- **Risk — multi-hit semantics:** shield must absorb exactly one hit; an
  over-eager base default could absorb repeatedly. Mitigated by AC2 (second hit
  must land).
- **Risk — phase vs invulnerability interaction:** phase immunity and the
  post-hit blink must not mask each other; covered by AC1/AC4 and existing
  PlayScene tests.
- **Risk — scope creep:** other effect/visual divergences may be discovered;
  record these as linked work items rather than expanding this fix.
- **Non-goal:** reworking the power-up spawn/placement layer or the P4/P5/P7/P9
  effects (already working).

## Related work

- AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a
  shared core scene base class (parent; completed). This bug is a gap in that
  consolidation: the hit-gating hooks were left as per-scene overrides.
- AH-0MUD9R3NB0093CBV — Extract player-hit lifecycle into CombatScene
  (completed) — the extraction that left `isPlayerPhased`/`tryAbsorbPlayerHit`
  abstract-per-scene.
- AH-0MUD9R3ZC0006M4I — Extract collision core and host bullet-vs-bullet impact
  feedback (completed).
- AH-0MTE8EBAH007GUO0 — Effects module: shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift,
  teleport (completed).
- AH-0MTE8EBG3004QC66 — Combat gym scene: GymPowerUpsCombat with ship, scouts,
  spawner, effects (completed).
- AH-0MTE8EC2W004MPUW — Unit tests: hit response, collection gate, round-robin
  spawner (completed).
- AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4 — Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies)
  (completed); AH-0MTHG5JVP006U6K7 — Retire per-enemy gym scenes (completed).
- AH-0MU8QV3O9008JVNQ — PlayScene: add P3 shield bubble visual + post-absorb
  blink (completed) — the visual parity this item extends to the gyms.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (approach):** Should the fix centralise phase/shield hit-gating in the
  shared combat base (and de-duplicate `PlayScene`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`), or add
  local overrides only to `GymFormationScene`?
  — **Recommended:** centralise in the shared base — matches the operator's
  explicit "ensure shared code is used so behaviour is the same in all scenes".
  — **Answer (operator):** "continue" — proceeded with the recommended option.
  Source: interactive reply. Assumption recorded for review.
- **Q2 (scope/visual parity):** Should the fix also bring the shield-bubble and
  phase-ghost player visuals to `GymFormationScene`-based scenes, or only fix
  the hit-gating?
  — **Recommended:** include visual parity — the operator asked for the same
  behaviour in all scenes and the effect should be observable.
  — **Answer (operator):** "continue" — proceeded with the recommended option.
  Source: interactive reply. Assumption recorded for review.
- **Q3 (diver scope):** Is there a Diver-specific scene that needs a separate
  fix?
  — Resolved by repository inspection (no operator input needed): `GymIndex`
  routes every non-boss enemy config, including `diver`, to the single reusable
  `GymEnemies` scene; per-enemy gym scenes were retired
  (AH-0MTHG5JVP006U6K7). Fixing `GymFormationScene` covers the Diver and all
  other enemy keys, plus `GymBoss`/`GymMinerals`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM** – Test: Enemy mineral count and re-drop distribution (completed)
- **AH-0MTHG5JVP006U6K7** – Retire per-enemy gym scenes (thin wrappers or delete) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: behaviour, boots, boss, cause, code (+40 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: behaviour, boss, cause, code, collected (+39 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: behaviour, boots, boss, cause, code (+34 more)

## Plan changelog

- **2026-09-26 (plan skill, session herdr-1790424231-1734441-12458):** decomposed into five child work items (test-first):
  - AH-0MUICQBE5007AIRU — Add enemy-gym phase/shield gating regression tests (task; AC1/AC2/AC6).
  - AH-0MUICQBQL002H0IW — Centralise phase/shield hit-gating in shared combat base (feature; AC2/AC3/AC7).
  - AH-0MUICQC34005QOYF — Add shield bubble and phase ghost to GymFormationScene (feature; AC4).
  - AH-0MUICQCEZ006Y4AA — Cross-scene equivalence and duplicate-body verification (task; AC3/AC7).
  - AH-0MUICQCQM002WAAJ — Document shared shield/phase gating (docs; AC5).
- Dependency edges: C2 depends on C1; C3 depends on C2; C4 depends on C2 and C3; C5 depends on C2.
- Reflowed the acceptance-criteria bullets onto single lines only (no wording change) so the shared AC-coverage helper can parse each criterion; the AC-coverage review then reports `proceed` with all 7 parent ACs covered.
- Appendix revision: no new questions were asked in this planning session. The Q1/Q2 answers ("continue" on the recommended shared-base and visual-parity options) and the repository-resolved Q3 remain the governing decisions; the decomposition above implements them.

# Ability items not functioning: Dual Shot, Teleport, Phase Shift

## Problem statement

Three collectable effects granted through the mineral hold-full reward flow do
not behave as the Game Design Document (GDD §2.3/§4.4/§4.5) describes:
**Dual Shot** (weapon drop) does not take effect in the main game, and
**P7 Teleport** and **P6 Phase Shift** are inert when collected in the
minerals gym. Repo investigation shows these are three distinct defects with
two shared root causes (choice display/apply divergence; mineral-gym combat
effects not wired), not cosmetic/reskin issues.

## Users

- **As a player in the main game**, when my mineral hold fills I want the
  power-up/weapon I pick in the "HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP" overlay to be
  the exact one applied, so my choice is honoured.
- **As a player in the minerals gym**, when a mineral reward grants me
  P7 Teleport I want S/↓ to consume a stored use and warp me to safety, so the
  reward is usable.
- **As a player in the minerals gym**, when a mineral reward grants me
  P6 Phase Shift (or P3 Shield) I want the intangibility/absorption to
  actually protect me, so the reward is usable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Displayed choice equals applied choice (main game + gyms).**
  When the hold-full choice overlay is shown, the option label the player
  selects is the exact option applied. Verified by a deterministic test
  (injected strategy + seeded RNG) that stubs `MineralChoiceScene` display
  options and asserts the option returned by `selectMineralChoice` equals the
  option shown/selected at the same index.
- **AC2 — P7 Teleport works in the minerals gym.** After a P7 Teleport is
  granted via the hold-full choice in `GymMinerals`, pressing S (or ↓)
  consumes one stored use, moves the player to the resolved safe spot, and
  grants P6 Phase Shift. Verified by a `GymMinerals` test that applies P7 via
  the choice path, invokes the teleport key/`triggerTeleport`, and asserts:
  stack decremented, player position changed, `registry.isPhased === true`.
- **AC3 — P6 Phase Shift protects in the minerals gym.** While P6 is active,
  enemy bullets and enemy bodies do not register a hit. Verified by a
  `GymMinerals` test that activates P6, places a bullet/body on the player, and
  asserts `playerHitCount` is unchanged.
- **AC4 — P3 Shield absorbs in the minerals gym (scope assumption, see
  below).** While P3 is active, the first hit is absorbed, the shield pops,
  and `playerHitCount` is unchanged; the next hit registers. Verified by test.
- **AC5 — No regression in existing power-up flows.** The full power-up gym
  (`GymPowerUpsCombat`), utility gym, and main-game teleport/phase/shield paths
  continue to pass their existing suites.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries (in particular the GDD §4.5 hold-full choice and §6.4 gym behaviour
  notes if wording drifts).
- **AC7 — Validation.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Teleport activation keys are fixed by the GDD: **S / ↓**.
- Must not regress `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `PlayScene`, or
  `PauseScene` pause/resume semantics.
- The choice overlay must remain pointer- and keyboard-operable (numbered keys
  and click), and must keep its opaque backdrop / z-order behaviour.
- All implementation must occur in the worktree created by
  `implement.py start AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` (implement skill), with
  build → test → commit ordering.

## Existing state (root-cause analysis from repo investigation)

1. **Main-game choice display/apply divergence (Dual Shot symptom).**
   `PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` stores
   `this.mineralChoiceOptions = this.mineralChoiceStrategy.choose(3, this.rng)`
   and then launches the overlay with only `{ origin: 'PlayScene' }`
   (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`). `MineralChoiceScene.init()` therefore draws its
   **own, independent** options via `randomChoiceStrategy.choose(3)`
   (`src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`). `MineralChoiceScene.select(index)`
   forwards only the **index** to `play.selectMineralChoice(index)`, which
   applies `play.mineralChoiceOptions[index]` — a different draw from the label
   shown. The player can therefore pick the displayed "Dual Shot" and have a
   different (often invisible/inert) option applied. The gym path does not have
   this bug because `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice()` passes `options`
   and an `onSelect` callback.

2. **P7 Teleport inert in the minerals gym.**
   `GymMinerals`'s `asteroidFormationConfig()` omits the `powerUps` config key,
   so `GymFormationScene.powerUpsEnabled` stays `false`. Consequently:
   `_initPowerUpLayer()` returns early and **never binds** the S/↓ keys;
   `_updatePowerUpLayer()` returns early and **never calls** `_handleTeleport()`;
   and `canTeleport()` returns `powerUpsEnabled` (`false`). P7 stacks granted
   via the hold-full choice can never be consumed. (`GymPowerUpsCombat` binds
   the keys and overrides the hooks, which is why it works there.)

3. **P6 Phase Shift / P3 Shield inert in the minerals gym.**
   `GymFormationScene` does **not** override `isPlayerPhased()` or
   `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()`, so `CombatCoreScene`'s defaults (`false`) are used
   even though `EffectsRegistry.isPhased` / `isShielded` are `true`. The
   mineral reward can grant these effects, but `_handleCollisions()` never
   honours them. (`GymPowerUpsCombat` and `PlayScene` override both hooks.)

4. Working reference implementations already exist for all three fixes:
   `GymPowerUpsCombat` (key binding, `isPlayerPhased`, `tryAbsorbPlayerHit`),
   `PlayScene` (phase/shield/teleport), and the gym choice path
   (`options` + `onSelect`).

## Desired change

- Make the hold-full choice a single source of truth so the option displayed is
  the option applied in `PlayScene` (and keep the gym's `options`/`onSelect`
  path working).
- Make P7 Teleport operational in `GymMinerals`: bind S/↓ and run
  `_handleTeleport()` whenever a player exists and a teleport stack is stored,
  independent of the opt-in power-up **drop** layer; allow
  `canTeleport()` when `hasTeleport()` is true.
- Wire the shared `EffectsRegistry` into `GymFormationScene`'s combat hooks so
  P6 (and P3) granted via the mineral reward choice are honoured
  (`isPlayerPhased()` → `registry.isPhased`; `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` → shield pop).
- Add the regression tests in the ACs above.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `openMineralChoice()` must pass the stored
  `mineralChoiceOptions` (and the active strategy) to the overlay so display and
  apply agree.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — accept the caller-supplied options
  consistently; optionally forward the selected `ChoiceOption` alongside the
  index.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — bind teleport keys whenever a
  player is present; call `_handleTeleport()` each tick independent of the
  power-up drop layer; permit `canTeleport()` when a stack is stored; override
  `isPlayerPhased()` and `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` to read the registry.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — config check; no change expected if the base
  scene is fixed, but confirm the mineral gym opts in to the teleport/hook
  behaviour.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` —
  review hook defaults only if a base-level (non-gym) fix is cleaner.
- Tests: `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts` (new cases), plus any shared-hook tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — *Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold and grant a power-up choice* (parent feature; defines the
  hold-full choice contract this work fixes).
- **AH-0MUCST2VY004T6QQ** — *Test: Hold-full choice scene and PlayScene wiring*
  (test contract for the choice overlay; does not cover the display/apply index
  divergence).
- **AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U** — *Redesign P7 Dash: make collectable teleport
  power-up* (P7 semantics: stored FIFO, S/↓, P6 on arrival).
- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** — *Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled
  power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7)* (reference implementation in `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- **AH-0MU8QVC9Y008R8I5** — *PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual*
  (PlayScene phase visual; confirms phase is functional there).
- Automated related-work report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "minerals gym" means `GymMinerals` (asteroids +
  mineral hold), not `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Evidence: the user distinguished
  "the main game" from "the minerals gym", and `GymMinerals` is the gym that
  offers the hold-full mineral reward choice without field power-up drops.
- **Assumption (scope):** P3 Shield and any other combat power-up granted via
  the mineral reward choice in `GymMinerals` are in scope because they share
  the `isPlayerPhased`/`tryAbsorbPlayerHit` root cause. If the producer wants
  the narrower fix only, drop AC4. **OPEN QUESTION** (see Appendix).
- **Risk:** S is also the "down" movement key in the 4-directional scheme;
  adding teleport binding to `GymMinerals` must use `JustDown` semantics so it
  never fires continuously while moving down, and must not double-consume
  stacks.
- **Risk:** fixing the main-game choice changes the effective option pool
  semantics (the drawn options become authoritative); tests must inject a
  deterministic strategy/RNG to avoid flakiness.
- **Risk:** a base-level change to `GymFormationScene` could regress gyms that
  rely on `powerUpsEnabled` gating (e.g. `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`). Mitigation:
  gate teleport on `hasTeleport()` rather than on the drop layer, and run the
  full gym suites.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any other defects found while fixing (e.g. HUD display
  of permanent weapons, shield bubble in `GymMinerals`) should be recorded as
  separate linked work items (`discovered-from:AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4`), not
  expanded into this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which gym is the "minerals gym"?** — Answer (agent research, from repo):
  `GymMinerals`, key `GymMinerals` (asteroids-only + 100 seeded minerals + the
  hold-full choice). Evidence: `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`,
  `GymFormationScene._initMineralLayer`, and the distinct
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`/`GymPowerUpsUtility` scenes.
- **Q: Is the "Dual Shot" symptom caused by the displayed-vs-applied option
  divergence?** — Answer (agent research, from repo): yes, the main-game path
  draws options twice (`PlayScene.openMineralChoice` and
  `MineralChoiceScene.init`) and applies by index only. Evidence:
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1902`, `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts:38,104`.
- **Q: Should P3 Shield (and other combat effects) granted via the mineral
  choice in `GymMinerals` also be fixed?** — Answer (assumed): yes, same root
  cause; documented in AC4. **OPEN QUESTION** for producer confirmation — the
  operator report named only Teleport and Phase Shift.
- **Q: Are field power-up drops expected in `GymMinerals`?** — Answer (agent
  research, from repo): no; the gym omits the `powerUps` config and relies on
  the mineral hold-full choice to grant effects. The fix must therefore not
  require enabling the full drop layer.

## Goal
Fix the displayed-vs-applied option divergence in the main-game mineral choice overlay so the player sees and gets the same option.

## Root Cause
`PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` draws options via `this.mineralChoiceStrategy.choose(3, this.rng)` and stores them in `this.mineralChoiceOptions`, but only passes `{ origin: 'PlayScene' }` to the MineralChoiceScene overlay. `MineralChoiceScene.init()` then draws its own independent options via `randomChoiceStrategy.choose(3)` when `options` is absent. `selectMineralChoice(index)` applies `play.mineralChoiceOptions[index]` — a different draw from the label shown.

## Implementation
1. In `PlayScene.openMineralChoice()`: pass `options: [...this.mineralChoiceOptions]` and `strategy: this.mineralChoiceStrategy` to MineralChoiceScene.init().
2. Confirm `MineralChoiceScene.init()` uses the passed options when present (already does: `data.options ?? strategy.choose(3)`).
3. Optionally forward the full `ChoiceOption` object from select() (not just index) for robustness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Displayed choice equals applied choice (main game + gyms):** deterministic test asserts selectMineralChoice returns the option shown at the same index.
- **AC-F1:** When PlayScene opens the mineral choice, the displayed options match `this.mineralChoiceOptions`.
- **AC-F2:** Selecting an option by index applies the correct stored option.
- **AC-F3:** The gym path (which already passes options) is unaffected.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — openMineralChoice()
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — init(), select()

## Goal
Make P7 Teleport operational in the minerals gym by wiring key binding, handler invocation, and canTeleport override.

## Root Cause
GymMinerals' asteroidFormationConfig() omits the `powerUps` config key, so GymFormationScene.powerUpsEnabled stays false. Consequently:
- _initPowerUpLayer() returns early and never binds the S/keys
- _updatePowerUpLayer() returns early and never calls _handleTeleport()
- canTeleport() returns powerUpsEnabled (false)

## Implementation
1. In GymFormationScene, bind the teleport key (S/Down) whenever a player exists, independent of powerUpsEnabled.
2. In GymFormationScene, call _handleTeleport() each tick whenever hasTeleport() is true, independent of powerUpsEnabled.
3. Override canTeleport() to return hasTeleport() in addition to powerUpsEnabled.
4. Ensure _handleTeleport() triggers P6 Phase Shift on arrival (as per GDD and AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U).

## Risks
- S is also the "down" movement key; use JustDown semantics to avoid double-consumption.
- Must not affect other gyms that rely on powerUpsEnabled gating.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC2 — P7 Teleport works in the minerals gym:** after a P7 Teleport is granted, stack decremented, player position changed, isPhased true.
- **AC-F4:** Pressing S or Down consumes one teleport stack and moves the player to a safe spot.
- **AC-F5:** P6 Phase Shift is granted on arrival.
- **AC-F6:** No regression in other gyms (GymPowerUpsCombat, GymEnemies, GymBoss).

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — _initPowerUpLayer, _updatePowerUpLayer, canTeleport, _handleTeleport
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/EffectsRegistry.ts`

## Goal
Wire the shared EffectsRegistry into GymFormationScene's combat hooks so P6 (Phase Shift) and P3 (Shield) granted via the mineral reward choice are honoured.

## Root Cause
GymFormationScene does not override isPlayerPhased() or tryAbsorbPlayerHit(), so CombatCoreScene's defaults (false) are used even though EffectsRegistry.isPhased / isShielded are true. The mineral reward can grant these effects, but _handleCollisions() never honours them.

## Implementation
1. Override isPlayerPhased() in GymFormationScene to return registry.isPhased.
2. Override tryAbsorbPlayerHit() in GymFormationScene to:
   - Return true (absorb) when registry.isShielded is true and pop the shield.
   - Delegate to the parent/hook chain for other logic.
3. Follow the pattern from GymPowerUpsCombat.ts which already overrides these hooks correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC3 — P6 Phase Shift protects in the minerals gym:** while P6 is active, enemy bullets and bodies do not register a hit; playerHitCount unchanged.
- **AC4 — P3 Shield absorbs in the minerals gym:** first hit absorbed and shield pops, playerHitCount unchanged; next hit registers.
- **AC-F7:** While P6 Phase Shift is active, enemy bullets and bodies do not register hits.
- **AC-F8:** While P3 Shield is active, the first hit is absorbed and the shield pops; the next hit registers.
- **AC-F9:** No regression in other gyms (GymPowerUpsCombat, GymEnemies, GymBoss, PlayScene).

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — isPlayerPhased(), tryAbsorbPlayerHit()
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — hook invocation
- `src/scenes/core/EffectsRegistry.ts` — isPhased, isShielded
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — reference implementation

# Add enemy-gym phase/shield gating regression tests

## Context

Parent: AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV — Enemy gym: P3 shield and P6 phase shift do not work when collected (hit-gating not shared).

Test-first slice of the parent bug. In `GymFormationScene` (the base of `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`) the inherited `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` defaults return `false`, so P6 Phase Shift and P3 Shield collected in the enemy gym are recorded in the `EffectsRegistry` (the HUD shows them active) but never gate a hit. This item adds the regression tests that prove the gap and become the red-to-green proof for the sibling implementation item.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want failing regression tests that pin the expected enemy-gym behaviour for P3/P6, so the fix cannot silently regress again and a fix in one scene cannot silently miss the others.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — P6 phase immunity in the enemy gym: with the power-up layer active in a `GymFormationScene`-based scene (any `enemyKey`, including `diver`), collecting P6 Phase Shift makes the player immune to enemy bullets and enemy body contact for the effect duration (no `playerHitCount` increment, no life loss, no respawn); on expiry the next hit lands normally.
- [ ] AC2 — P3 shield absorbs one hit in the enemy gym: collecting P3 Shield causes exactly the next hit to be absorbed — the shield is consumed (registry no longer shielded), the post-hit invulnerability window starts, and the player does not lose a life; the following hit lands normally.
- [ ] AC6 — validation: an automated test/validation criterion is satisfied across the affected scenes (new regression tests fail before the fix and pass after it); the red evidence is recorded in a work-item comment.
- [ ] The tests exercise a real enemy key route (`GymEnemies` with `enemyKey: 'diver'`) and/or a `GymFormationScene` stub, so the single reusable enemy gym scene is covered.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — behavioural regression tests on the stub formation scene with the power-up layer enabled.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — diver-route regression test on the real reusable enemy gym scene.

## Deliverables

- New and updated tests only (no production code changes in this item).

# Centralise phase/shield hit-gating in shared combat base

## Context

Parent: AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV — Enemy gym: P3 shield and P6 phase shift do not work when collected (hit-gating not shared).

`PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` each override `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()`; `GymFormationScene` does not, so it inherits `CombatCoreScene`'s `false` defaults and the enemy gym never gates a hit. Move the registry-backed gating into one shared place so every `CombatScene` subclass cannot diverge.

## User story

As a maintainer, I expect phase/shield hit-gating to live in one shared place, so a fix in one scene cannot silently miss the others.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC3 — single shared implementation: phase/shield hit-gating is implemented once in the shared combat base (`CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`) backed by the inherited `EffectsRegistry`; the now-redundant duplicate overrides in `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` are removed or reduced to scene-specific extras, and an equivalence test asserts `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` route phase/shield through the same shared hooks.
- [ ] AC2 — P3 shield absorbs one hit in the enemy gym: the shield absorb consumes exactly one shield, starts the post-hit invulnerability, and never costs a life; the following hit lands normally; invulnerability durations are preserved (`PlayScene` 1.5 s, `GymPowerUpsCombat` 0.8 s) and the unabsorbed hit still runs the normal lose-life flow.
- [ ] AC7 — full suite: full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] `GymFormationScene` and its subclasses (`GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`) inherit correct gating with no per-scene override.
- [ ] The play scene's shield-absorb destruction cue is preserved via a scene-specific hook (for example `onShieldAbsorbed()` default no-op) so `GymPowerUpsCombat` behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] The regression tests from the test-first sibling item pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — concrete registry-backed hooks plus an optional `onShieldAbsorbed()` seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — update hook docs; keep safe non-combat defaults for direct subclasses (`GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeapons`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — remove the two overrides; keep the absorb cue via the seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — remove the two overrides.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — unit tests for the shared hooks.

## Deliverables

- Production code plus updated unit tests.

# Add shield bubble and phase ghost to GymFormationScene

## Context

Parent: AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV — Enemy gym: P3 shield and P6 phase shift do not work when collected (hit-gating not shared).

Even once gating is fixed, `GymFormationScene` draws no P3 shield bubble and no P6 phase ghost, so the active effect is invisible in the enemy gym, unlike `PlayScene` / `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Add the same player visuals for parity.

## User story

As a player training in the enemy gym, when P3 Shield or P6 Phase Shift is active I expect the same shield bubble and phase ghost cue as in the real run, so I can see the effect is active.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC4 — consistent player feedback: `GymFormationScene`-based scenes render the same shield-bubble (P3) and phase-ghost (P6) player visuals as `PlayScene`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`, so the active effect is observable in the enemy gym.
- [ ] Shield bubble parameters: colour `0x3399ff`, line width 2, radius `SHIP_SIZE * 1.6`, fill alpha 0.12; drawn around the ship while `getEffectsRegistry().isShielded` is true and cleared when not shielded.
- [ ] Phase ghost alpha 0.45 while `getEffectsRegistry().isPhased` is true and not in the invulnerability blink, alpha 1 otherwise; safe when no player is present.
- [ ] The visual update runs from the scene per-frame `tick` path.
- [ ] The same drawing parameters are used by `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene` (preferably through one shared helper) so the three scenes cannot drift visually.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — shield-bubble and phase-ghost rendering, wired into the per-frame tick.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — visual parity tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — optional shared visual helper (new file) if extraction is cheap; otherwise keep the parameters documented and identical.

## Deliverables
